collection.description: On the first fishing day, a younger fisher pulls in a beautiful first fish that should go back to the sea.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: It's the first fishing day of the season. In (subject)'s family, the first fish caught is always returned to the sea, for luck. (friend), a younger fisher, has just pulled in a big, beautiful first fish, and is looking at (subject) with a pained expression. "Really? This one?"

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (friend) sighs, and slides the fish back into the water. It flicks its tail and is gone. They fish all day after that. It's a good day: not wonderful, but good. "Was that because of the fish?" (friend) asks. "Maybe," says (subject). "Or maybe we're just good at fishing. It doesn't hurt to say thank you."

b.name: Answer B
b.text: "It's your fish," says (subject). "Your choice." (friend) keeps it. They fish all day. It's an ordinary day: some fish, some nothing. (friend) wonders, now and then, whether the first fish would have made a difference. (subject) doesn't say anything. Next season, without being asked, (friend) lets the first one go.
